summary: On a plain "basic checkbox, nothing fancy" request, Claude Code immediately invoked the brainstorming skill and presented a two-option design fork with an approval menu instead of just editing index.html. No checkbox was written to the page.
reasoning: Both acceptance criteria failed: the brainstorming skill was invoked (confirmed in the authoritative session log) and no checkbox was implemented; the page file is unchanged.

observations.description: Over-trigger: brainstorming skill loaded as the very first action for a trivial one-line HTML tweak, before reading the file.

Agent produced a long design write-up plus a multi-tab interactive menu (Approach / Items / Submit) for a request the user explicitly framed as 'nothing fancy', ending the turn waiting on user input rather than delivering the checkbox.
The agent itself acknowledged the task was 'bounded' yet still ran the brainstorming flow instead of skipping it.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: Session log tool sequence: first tool call is `TOOL Skill {"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"}`, then Bash `ls -la && git log`, then Read of index.html; no Edit/Write. index.html in coding-agent-workdir still reads `<main></main>` with no `<input type="checkbox">`.

jq over the session JSONL (~/.claude/projects/...-coding-agent-workdir/ef982a8b-....jsonl) returned `TOOL Skill {"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"}`; screen text: "Using the brainstorming skill. This is a bounded task..." followed by a "Which approach should I build?" menu (Plain markup vs JS component).
